newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala government says kidnappings way down.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala government says kidnappings way down.

text.p: A community crime group provided Guatemalan newspapers a list of 229 people it says have been kidnapped this year, but the government said on Thursday there was only one confirmed case.
The grassroots anti-crime group, Neighbourhood Guardians, gave the list to newspapers as part of a campaign to urge the government to admit kidnapping is still a problem.
But police say that the number has dropped dramatically since mid-1996 when reported abductions for profit peaked at three a day.

"We are working on four unsolved cases left over from last year but only one new case has been reported this year and that man is safely back at home," Deputy Interior Minister Salvador Gandara told reporters at a news conference.
"We have determined that most of these cases are totally false," Gandara said.
National Police Chief Angel Conte said many of the people on the list had been reported as missing, but that police investigations determined they were not being held for ransom.

The list contains names of men evading arrest warrants, women who left home and became prostitutes, women who abandoned their husbands and joined religious cults, a shoeshine boy who still works at his usual post in front of a provincial police headquarters, and people who had simply moved, Conte said.
Hundreds of kidnappings were reported in 1996 and army and police personnel and ex-guerrillas, as well as criminals, were linked to cases.

Oscar Recinos, leader of the Neighbourhood Guardians and a failed candidate for mayor of Guatemala City, has repeatedly berated the National Police for not revealing the true number of kidnappings it is investigating.
